children: , the cloud and enterprise-AI giant, expanded Copilot's push into app building and autonomous work, according to Reuters. Shares jumped nearly 3.6% to $515.64 as of 10.11am ET time this morning. The next test is simple: turn more AI capabilities into revenue customers are willing to keep paying for.

Code will let users create dashboards and applications with plain-language instructions, with early access starting this month. Autopilot will operate with a corporate-directory identity and administrator-set permissions. New spending controls will also show companies what employee AI usage costs. That puts IT managers at the center of the rollout: they control access, approve spending and decide whether the productivity gains justify the bill.

The valuation graphic puts Microsoft 12.22% below its $587.39 GF Value estimate as of September 25, 2026, suggesting a valuation cushion rather than a guaranteed bargain. The business still has to deliver. More agents could lift subscription revenue and consumption, but tighter customer budgets could limit that upside. title: Microsoft Jumps Nearly 3.6% as Copilot Becomes a Digital Coworker
